    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def agent(name: str, description: str) -> str:
    return f"---\nname: {name}\nrole: Example\nmodel: sonnet\neffort: medium\ndescription: >-\n  {description}\n---\n\nBody.\n"


def skill(name: str, description: str, version: str = "1.0.0") -> str:
    return f"---\nname: {name}\ndescription: {description}\nversion: {version}\n---\n\nBody.\n"


class PlatformLimitTests(unittest.TestCase):

        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.directory.cleanup)

        write(self.root, "plugins/alpha/agents/worker.md", agent("worker", "Does the work."))
        write(self.root, "plugins/alpha/skills/run/SKILL.md", skill("run", "Runs the pipeline."))
        write(self.root, "plugins/beta/agents/judge.md", agent("judge", "Judges the result."))
        write(self.root, "plugins/beta/skills/check/SKILL.md", skill("check", "Checks the result."))

    def test_folded_frontmatter_values_are_joined(self) -> None:
        meta = limits.parse_frontmatter(agent("worker", "First part second part."))
        self.assertEqual(meta["description"], "First part second part.")
        self.assertEqual(meta["name"], "worker")

    def test_existing_references_resolve(self) -> None:
        write(self.root, "plugins/alpha/README.md", "Hand off to `beta:judge`, then run beta/check and alpha:run.\n")
        self.assertEqual(limits.check_cross_references(self.root), [])

    def test_missing_references_are_reported_with_file_and_line(self) -> None:
        write(self.root, "plugins/alpha/README.md", "Intro.\nSee `beta:referee` for judgment.\nOr beta/verify.\n")

        self.assertEqual(len(failures), 2)
        self.assertIn("plugins/alpha/README.md:2", failures[0])
        self.assertIn("beta:referee", failures[0])
        self.assertIn("beta/verify", failures[1])

    def test_negative_statements_and_paths_are_not_references(self) -> None:
        write(
            self.root,
            "plugins/alpha/README.md",
            "There is no separate beta/verify skill to invoke.\nSee ../beta/ and plugins/beta/agents and https://example.com/beta/page.\n",
        )
        self.assertEqual(limits.check_cross_references(self.root), [])

    def test_description_budget_fails_only_above_the_threshold(self) -> None:
        failures, summary = limits.check_description_budget(self.root)
        self.assertEqual(failures, [])
        self.assertIn("2 agent descriptions", summary)
        write(self.root, "plugins/alpha/agents/huge.md", agent("huge", "x" * (12_000 * 4)))
        failures, _ = limits.check_description_budget(self.root)
        self.assertEqual(len(failures), 1)

    def test_skill_name_and_length_are_checked(self) -> None:
        write(self.root, "plugins/alpha/skills/wrong/SKILL.md", skill("other-name", "Fine."))
        write(self.root, "plugins/alpha/skills/long/SKILL.md", skill("long", "x" * 1_025))
        failures = limits.check_skill_metadata(self.root)
        self.assertEqual(len(failures), 2)
        self.assertTrue(any("must equal its directory name" in failure for failure in failures))
        self.assertTrue(any("1025 characters" in failure for failure in failures))

    def test_codex_budget(self) -> None:
        write(self.root, "harnesses/codex/plugins/alpha/skills/run/SKILL.md", skill("run", "x" * 8_001))
        failures, _ = limits.check_codex_budget(self.root)
        self.assertEqual(len(failures), 1)

    def test_the_repository_passes_its_own_checks(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(limits.check_cross_references(REPOSITORY_ROOT), [])
        self.assertEqual(limits.check_skill_metadata(REPOSITORY_ROOT), [])
        self.assertEqual(limits.check_description_budget(REPOSITORY_ROOT)[0], [])
        self.assertEqual(limits.check_codex_budget(REPOSITORY_ROOT)[0], [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Cover tools/transcript-metrics.py on synthetic transcripts and verdict files."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPOSITORY_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TOOL = REPOSITORY_ROOT / "tools" / "transcript-metrics.py"

specification = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("transcript_metrics", TOOL)
assert specification is not None and specification.loader is not None
metrics = importlib.util.module_from_spec(specification)
specification.loader.exec_module(metrics)


def assistant(*blocks: dict) -> dict:
    return {"type": "assistant", "message": {"content": list(blocks)}}


def tool_use(identifier: str, name: str, **input_fields) -> dict:
    return {"type": "tool_use", "id": identifier, "name": name, "input": input_fields}


def tool_result(identifier: str, content, agent_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
    record = {"type": "user", "message": {"content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": identifier, "content": content}]}}
    if agent_id:
        record["toolUseResult"] = {"agentId": agent_id}
    return record


def notification(task: str, tokens: int, duration_ms: int) -> dict:
    text = (
        f"<task-notification><task-id>{task}</task-id><status>completed</status>"
        f"<usage><subagent_tokens>{tokens}</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>3</tool_uses>"
        f"<duration_ms>{duration_ms}</duration_ms></usage></task-notification>"
    )
    return {"type": "user", "message": {"content": text}}


class TranscriptMetricsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.directory.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.directory.name)
        project = self.root / "projects" / "-Users-x-Projects-site"
        project.mkdir(parents=True)
        lines = [
            assistant(tool_use("t1", "Agent", subagent_type="muse:exit-gate"), tool_use("t2", "Agent", subagent_type="fork")),
            tool_result("t1", "started", agent_id="a1"),
            tool_result("t2", "started", agent_id="a2"),
            notification("a1", 250_000, 120_000),
            notification("a1", 250_000, 120_000),  # repeated in the transcript, counted once
            notification("a2", 100_000, 60_000),
            assistant(tool_use("s1", "Skill", skill="muse:component"), tool_use("b1", "Bash", command="ls"), tool_use("r1", "Read", file_path="x")),
            tool_result("s1", "loaded"),
            tool_result("b1", "x" * 900),
            tool_result("r1", [{"type": "text", "text": "y" * 100}]),
            {"type": "user", "message": {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "<command-name>/resume</command-name>"}]}},
        ]
        (project / "abcdef1234.jsonl").write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(line) for line in lines), encoding="utf-8")
        self.projects = self.root / "projects"
        self.files = metrics.session_files(self.projects, "site$")

    def test_agents_dedupes_notifications_and_splits_plugin_from_other(self) -> None:
        report = metrics.command_agents(self.files, cliff=200_000)
        gate = report["types"][("abcdef12", "muse:exit-gate")]
        self.assertEqual((gate["calls"], gate["tokens"], gate["minutes"]), (1, 250_000, 2.0))
        self.assertEqual((report["plugin_tokens"], report["other_tokens"]), (250_000, 100_000))
        self.assertEqual(report["over_cliff"], [("abcdef12", "muse:exit-gate", 250_000)])

    def test_skills_counts_skill_agent_and_command_invocations(self) -> None:
        report = metrics.command_skills(self.files)["abcdef12"]
        self.assertEqual(report["skills"], {"muse:component": 1})
        self.assertEqual(report["agents"], {"muse:exit-gate": 1, "fork": 1})
        self.assertEqual(report["commands"], {"resume": 1})

    def test_outputs_share_and_ceiling(self) -> None:
        report = metrics.command_outputs(self.files, "Bash", 0.5)
        self.assertEqual(report["by_tool"]["Bash"], 900)
        self.assertEqual(report["by_tool"]["Read"], 100)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(report["tool_share"], 900 / (900 + 100 + len("started") * 2 + len("loaded")), places=3)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(report["ceiling_of_tool_output"], report["tool_share"] * 0.5, places=3)

    def test_gates_report_rounds_retry_cap_long_summaries_and_escalation(self) -> None:
        directory = self.root / "specs"
        directory.mkdir()

        def verdict(name: str, **fields) -> None:
            (directory / name).write_text(json.dumps({"verdict": "fail", "blockers": [], **fields}), encoding="utf-8")

        verdict("SPEC-1-verdict.json", blockers=[{"criterion": "a", "finding": "b"}], retry_count=1)
        verdict("SPEC-1-verdict-2.json", retry_count=4, verdict_summary="x" * 301)
        verdict("SPEC-1-verdict-10.json", verdict="pass", retry_count=5)
        verdict("SPEC-2-verdict.json", blockers=[{"criterion": "escalation_required", "finding": "cap"}])
        report = metrics.command_gates(directory)
        first = report["SPEC-1"]
        self.assertEqual(first["rounds"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(first["verdicts"], ["fail", "fail", "pass"])  # rounds sort numerically, so 10 follows 2
        self.assertEqual(first["final"], "pass")
        self.assertEqual(first["blockers_per_round"], [1, 0, 0])
        self.assertEqual((first["max_retry_count"], first["over_retry_cap"], first["long_summaries"]), (5, 2, 1))
        self.assertEqual(report["SPEC-2"]["escalations"], 1)

    def test_command_line_runs_and_rejects_nothing_silently(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(metrics.main(["agents", "--projects-dir", str(self.projects), "--match", "site$"]), 0)
        self.assertEqual(metrics.main(["gates", str(self.root / "no-such-directory")]), 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Check tools/paired-analysis.py against hand-computed statistics and the pairing rules."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
import math
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPOSITORY_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TOOL = REPOSITORY_ROOT / "tools" / "paired-analysis.py"

specification = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("paired_analysis", TOOL)
assert specification is not None and specification.loader is not None
analysis = importlib.util.module_from_spec(specification)
specification.loader.exec_module(analysis)


def trial(task: str, arm: str, run: int = 1, error: bool = False, **fields) -> dict:
    return {"task": task, "arm": arm, "run": run, "error": error, **fields}


class StatisticsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_sign_test_matches_the_exact_binomial(self) -> None:
        self.assertAlmostEqual(analysis.sign_test(9, 1), 2 * (1 + 10) / 1024)
        self.assertEqual(analysis.sign_test(0, 0), 1.0)
        self.assertEqual(analysis.sign_test(5, 5), 1.0)

    def test_wilcoxon_exact_values(self) -> None:
        # all five differences positive: W+ = 15 is the maximum, P(W+ >= 15) = 1/32, two-sided 2/32
        self.assertAlmostEqual(analysis.wilcoxon_signed_rank([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), 2 / 32)
        # symmetric differences give the centre of the distribution
        self.assertEqual(analysis.wilcoxon_signed_rank([-1, 1]), 1.0)
        # zeros are dropped
        self.assertEqual(analysis.wilcoxon_signed_rank([0, 0, 0]), 1.0)
        # ties use average ranks: |d| = 1, 1, 2 -> ranks 1.5, 1.5, 3; all positive gives 2/8
        self.assertAlmostEqual(analysis.wilcoxon_signed_rank([1, 1, 2]), 2 / 8)

    def test_wilcoxon_normal_approximation_agrees_with_the_exact_limit(self) -> None:
        differences = [(-1) ** i * (i + 1) for i in range(40)]
        exact = analysis.wilcoxon_signed_rank(differences)
        analysis.EXACT_WILCOXON_LIMIT = 10
        try:
            approximate = analysis.wilcoxon_signed_rank(differences)
        finally:
            analysis.EXACT_WILCOXON_LIMIT = 60
        self.assertLess(abs(exact - approximate), 0.05)

    def test_cohen_kappa(self) -> None:
        self.assertAlmostEqual(analysis.cohen_kappa([(1, 1), (1, 0), (0, 0), (0, 0)]), 0.5)
        self.assertEqual(analysis.cohen_kappa([(1, 1), (0, 0)]), 1.0)
        self.assertTrue(math.isnan(analysis.cohen_kappa([])))


class ComparisonTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def trials(self) -> list[dict]:
        rows = []
        for index in range(1, 7):
            task = f"t{index}"
            rows.append(trial(task, "base", 1, score=0.5, cost=1.0))
            rows.append(trial(task, "base", 2, score=0.5, cost=3.0))
            rows.append(trial(task, "with", 1, score=0.5 + (0.25 if index <= 2 else 0), cost=1.1))
            rows.append(trial(task, "with", 2, score=0.5 + (0.25 if index <= 2 else 0), cost=1.3))
        rows.append(trial("crashed", "base", score=1.0, cost=1.0))
        rows.append(trial("crashed", "with", error=True))
        return rows

    def test_repeated_runs_reduce_to_a_median_and_crashes_drop_from_every_arm(self) -> None:
        report = analysis.compare(self.trials(), "base", ["score", "cost"])
        self.assertEqual((report["tasks"], report["paired"], report["excluded"]), (7, 6, 1))
        row = report["comparisons"]["with"]
        self.assertAlmostEqual(row["cost"]["median_delta"], 1.2 - 2.0)  # medians of two runs: 2.0 vs 1.2
        self.assertAlmostEqual(row["cost"]["median_relative_change"], (1.2 - 2.0) / 2.0)
        self.assertEqual((row["score"]["better"], row["score"]["worse"], row["score"]["tied"]), (2, 0, 4))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(row["score"]["sign_test_p"], 0.5)

    def test_unknown_baseline_is_an_error(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
            analysis.compare(self.trials(), "nope", ["score"])

    def test_three_arms_each_compare_with_the_baseline(self) -> None:
        trials = self.trials() + [trial(f"t{i}", "terse", score=0.5, cost=2.5) for i in range(1, 7)]
        report = analysis.compare(trials, "base", ["cost"])
        self.assertEqual(sorted(report["comparisons"]), ["terse", "with"])

    def test_command_line_reads_json_lines_and_lists(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            as_lines = Path(directory) / "trials.jsonl"
            as_lines.write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(row) for row in self.trials()), encoding="utf-8")
            as_list = Path(directory) / "trials.json"
            as_list.write_text(json.dumps(self.trials()), encoding="utf-8")
            self.assertEqual(len(analysis.load_trials(as_lines)), len(analysis.load_trials(as_list)))
            self.assertEqual(analysis.main(["compare", str(as_lines), "--baseline", "base", "--metrics", "score,cost"]), 0)

    def test_sign_test_matches_the_exact_binomial(self) -> None:
        self.assertAlmostEqual(analysis.sign_test(9, 1), 2 * (1 + 10) / 1024)
        self.assertEqual(analysis.sign_test(0, 0), 1.0)
        self.assertEqual(analysis.sign_test(5, 5), 1.0)

    def test_wilcoxon_exact_values(self) -> None:
        # all five differences positive: W+ = 15 is the maximum, P(W+ >= 15) = 1/32, two-sided 2/32
        self.assertAlmostEqual(analysis.wilcoxon_signed_rank([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]), 2 / 32)

        self.assertEqual(analysis.wilcoxon_signed_rank([-1, 1]), 1.0)
        # zeros are dropped

        # ties use average ranks: |d| = 1, 1, 2 -> ranks 1.5, 1.5, 3; all positive gives 2/8

            rows.append(trial(task, "base", 1, score=0.5, cost=1.0))
            rows.append(trial(task, "base", 2, score=0.5, cost=3.0))
            rows.append(trial(task, "with", 1, score=0.5 + (0.25 if index <= 2 else 0), cost=1.1))

# Evaluation methodology

How to decide whether a plugin, a skill, a prompt change or a token-saving tool actually helps. It applies to `mason:evaluate`, `claude plugin eval` and any ad hoc A/B run. The rules come from paired benchmarks of agent add-ons (the Caveman and rtk tests by JetBrains, the Netflix code-intelligence study) and from what went wrong in this repository's own sessions; the evidence is in `docs/evaluations/frontend-design/`.

## Rules

1. **Compare against a fair control.** Use at least three arms: no treatment, a plain control that gets the cheap version of the idea (for a brevity skill, "answer concisely"), and the treatment. A treatment compared only with an unconstrained baseline measures the idea, not your implementation of it.
2. **Pair by task and repeat.** Every arm runs the same tasks with the same model, effort, settings and budget. Run each task more than once; reduce repeats to a per-task median. A single run per task misleads: a first 10-task run reported a 30% token saving that fell to 8.5% at 86 tasks, and a +36% cost penalty fell to noise at three runs.
3. **Exclude a crashed task from every arm.** If a task has no successful trial in any arm, drop it from all arms and report how many were dropped. Never score a crash as zero in one arm only.
4. **Climb the ladder, cheapest first.** (a) Replay existing transcripts to bound what the idea could possibly touch, at no cost (`tools/transcript-metrics.py outputs`). (b) A one-trial wiring check that the treatment actually fires. (c) A small slice, one run. (d) The same slice with three runs. (e) The full set at each effort level you will use. Stop when a rung shows nothing.
5. **Measure the bill and the outcome, not the tool's own scoreboard.** A tool's self-reported saving is a claim about its counterfactual. rtk's scoreboard reported 96.2 million tokens saved while the measured cost went up. Use measured cost, turns and tokens, and a graded outcome.
6. **Grade outcomes mechanically where you can.** Task verifiers and hidden-oracle fixtures (`mason:evaluate`) come first. When an LLM judge is unavoidable, calibrate it: label at least 20 items by hand, run the judge on them, and report raw agreement and Cohen's kappa (`tools/paired-analysis.py agreement`). Treat a kappa below about 0.6 as a judge you cannot rely on; this threshold is a convention, not a measured result.
7. **Test at the effort you will run.** Effects reversed with effort: rtk cost +7.6% at low effort and no difference at high effort. Pin the model and effort in every arm and run each effort you intend to use.
8. **Watch the cost cliff.** A single long session can cross a long-context pricing tier and flip a total (one task billed $8.29 against $0.33). Report per-task medians and totals with and without outliers, and flag tasks above 200,000 reported tokens (`tools/transcript-metrics.py agents --cliff`).
9. **State the power.** About 80 paired tasks can only rule out large effects; catching a few-point shift needs on the order of hundreds of runs per arm. A null result is not proof of no effect. Say so in the report.
10. **Record provenance.** Model ids and versions, effort, plugin versions, source revision, the harness and its version, task set, number of runs, and the dates.

## Statistics

`tools/paired-analysis.py compare <trials> --baseline <arm>` implements rules 2, 3 and 9: per-task medians, an exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired differences (normal approximation above 60 pairs), the median relative change, and for the quality score an exact two-sided sign test with the counts of better, worse and tied tasks. It reads a JSON list or JSON Lines of trials with `task`, `arm`, `run`, optional `error`, and numeric fields such as `score`, `cost`, `turns`, `tokens`.

## Which tool for which question

| Question | Use |
| :-- | :-- |
| Does a plugin change behavior against no plugin, cheaply and in CI? | `claude plugin eval`: cases run with and without the plugin; it never fails on the difference, so read the difference yourself |
| Does a workflow find defects it should, with answers hidden from the agent, across harnesses? | `mason:evaluate` with hidden-oracle fixtures |
| What could a token-saving tool possibly reach? | Transcript replay first, then the ladder above |
| Did a change make agents cost more or run longer? | `tools/transcript-metrics.py agents` before and after, then a paired run |

See `docs/evaluations/frontend-design/investigations/plugin-eval-assessment.md` for how the two evaluation tools combine and for a first suite design.

## Report template

State the question, the arms, the tasks and runs, the model and effort, how crashes were handled, the paired medians with p-values, the outcome counts, the cost with and without outliers, the power note, and what would change the conclusion.

# Architecture assumptions register

Every part of a harness encodes an assumption about what the model cannot do on its own, and those assumptions go stale as models and hosts change. This register records each load-bearing assumption in `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the decision records, the evidence for and against it, and the check that would retire it. Review it when a new model generation ships, when Claude Code or Codex changes how agents, hooks or plugins work, and before a release. First version: 2026-10-20, from `docs/evaluations/frontend-design/ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md` after primary-source verification.

Status: **Holds**, **Changing** (a work package is in progress), **Open** (evidence is mixed; a measurement is planned), **Retire** (evidence says drop it).

| # | Assumption | Where it lives | Evidence now | Status | Next check |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 1 | Context is scarce, so load references on demand | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 1, `<load_first>` blocks | Skills are progressive disclosure natively; Anthropic's context guidance asks for the minimal sufficient information | Holds | Re-read when context-window or compaction behavior changes |
| 2 | One agent per cognitive mode | ADR 003, `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 7 | Anthropic recommends splitting by context isolation, not role, and multi-agent runs cost 3 to 15 times a single agent; verifier, adversary and recon splits are justified by independent context | Open | WP-605 classifies each of the 44 agents; WP-601 tests collapsed variants against a no-plugin baseline |
| 3 | A byte-identical constitution block is a shared cache prefix | ADR 006 | The block is 6 lines in each agent, so its cost is small; cache prefixes are shared only for the same model, effort, agent type, tools, schema and directory, with a 5-minute subagent TTL | Open | WP-604 measures sharing; no change unless a net benefit is shown |
| 4 | Capability tiers by model and effort | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5 | Effort is a native per-agent control; defaults and semantics differ by model; the Codex tiers were re-chosen by position and are unevaluated | Open | WP-63 sweeps effort at the effort actually run; re-check on each model release |
| 5 | JSON schemas are the inter-agent contract | ADR 004 | Portable across harnesses; recorded gate verdicts conform except one rule (summary length) | Holds | Enforce deterministically (WP-602) |
| 6 | The `reasoning` scratchpad field is safe | Constitution, 29 of 31 schemas | Documentation names such a field as a refusal trigger; a live probe on Sonnet 5.5 completed normally with the field and refused only a demand for verbatim reasoning; no refusals in 72k+ transcript messages | Holds | `tests/test_reasoning_wording.py` guards the wording; re-run the probe per model generation and on Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Haiku 5.5 (WP-625) |
| 7 | Default-fail gates with a retry cap of 3 and human escalation | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6 | The cap lived in a prompt and was not enforced: eight specs passed with `retry_count` 4 to 9; the `muse` gate told the agent to emit a verdict value no schema allows (fixed) | Changing | WP-602: enforce with a hook or workflow; the spike is `tools/validate-handback.py` |

| 9 | Work is a sequential pipeline of ten plugins | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 3 | Autonomous runs are getting longer and stage granularity tuned for short horizons goes stale; stages should be elidable | Open | WP-608, WP-18 (mode router) |
| 10 | Plans carry exact implementation code | navigator, ADR 009 | Anthropic kept its own planner at high-level design and says over-prescriptive guidance degrades newer models; large plans stalled agents | Open | WP-608: outcome-level plans |
| 11 | Verification evidence is text, code and tests | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4 | Every target harness has a native browser; one study found 44.5% of agent runs never looked at the design screenshots; visible defects shipped past every gate | Changing | WP-607, WP-40, WP-41 |
| 12 | Agents are stateless across sessions | no memory design | Decisions were lost between sessions; native memory, persistent plugin data and session search exist | Changing | WP-612, WP-13 |
| 13 | Two source trees, one lifecycle contract | `ARCHITECTURE.md` sections 8 to 10 | Codex has its own native plugin format set up in `harnesses/codex/`; Antigravity's format is similar to Claude Code's and shares the authored tree; Agent Plugins 1.0.0 standardizes a portable core | Holds | WP-610 |
| 14 | Humans approve through written artifacts | specs, verdicts | The user asked for rendered examples repeatedly and drawn prototypes exposed defects the gated spec missed | Changing | WP-34, WP-614 |

## How to update

Add a row when a decision record or architectural section introduces a new assumption. Change a status only with the evidence that moved it, citing a file in `docs/evaluations/` or a dated fact in `docs/verified-facts.md`. When a status becomes **Retire**, open or update the decision record that carries the assumption.

# Evidence quality convention

How to tag and weigh evidence when research, an evaluation or a decision record cites it. The aim is that a reader can tell, at a glance, how far a claim can be trusted and what would change it.

## Source tags

| Tag | Meaning |
| :-- | :-- |
| `P` | The primary page, file or dataset was read in full |
| `P*` | The primary page was read through a summarizing fetch; quotes may be paraphrased, so re-fetch before quoting in a decision record or the constitution |
| `F` | Measured or observed first-hand, with the method and the command or script that reproduces it |
| `S` | A search-result summary only; never enough to act on |
| `K` | The author's own knowledge, not fetched |
| `I` | Inference from other evidence; say which evidence |
| `U` | Unverified |

## Risk flags

Add a flag whenever one applies. A flagged claim can inform a decision but is not established by itself.

| Flag | Use when |
| :-- | :-- |
| `vendor-run` | The vendor measured its own product or published the case study |

Codex role cards are portable plugin resources. They are not TOML configuration: host TOML controls local runtime defaults and is never a marketplace contract.

Codex's own custom agents are TOML files (`.codex/agents/<name>.toml` with `name`, `description` and `developer_instructions`, and optionally a model and reasoning effort). A subagent inherits the parent's sandbox and approvals, and an agent file cannot override them, so a role card cannot make a role read-only by itself: the skill states the write boundary in its delegation packet and the primary agent checks the result. Codex also starts subagents only when the skill or the user asks, so a delegating skill must say which role to start and with what packet; "when teams are available" never triggers delegation. Whether to offer an optional, non-contract generator that turns role cards into TOML for users who want named Codex agents is an open decision (proposed decision record N8).

# Cross-Harness Authoring

Use this guide when a change affects Claude/AGY source plugins, Codex-native plugins, shared artifact contracts, or generated Codex distribution.

## Design boundary

Shared sources preserve lifecycle identity and interoperable artifacts. Harness sources preserve execution quality. Never mechanically translate prompts, model tiers, named agents, or delegation topology across harnesses.

| Concern | Shared source | Claude/AGY source | Codex source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Identity | ID, version, author, `consumes`, `produces` | Uses `plugins/<id>/plugin.json` | Native manifest matches ID, version, and author |
| Artifact contract | Versioned JSON schema | Produces and consumes the schema | Produces and consumes the same schema bytes |
| Skill inventory | Lifecycle route name | `plugins/<id>/skills/<skill>/` | Same route name under `harnesses/codex/plugins/<id>/skills/` |
| Workflow | None | Specialist agents and Claude-native orchestration | Native skill plus optional Codex role cards |
| Delegation | None | Named source agents | `agent-roles/<role>.md` selected only for bounded independent work |

Codex role cards are portable plugin resources. They are not TOML configuration: host TOML controls local runtime defaults and is never a marketplace contract.

## Change procedure

1. Classify the change before editing: shared identity, shared artifact contract, Claude/AGY workflow, Codex workflow, or distribution only.
2. Read the counterpart source before deciding whether it needs a change. Preserve lifecycle intent and artifact validity; do not preserve wording or topology by default.
3. For an identity or schema change, update the shared source first. Version an incompatible schema, update every affected producer and consumer, then update both harness workflows.
4. For a new or renamed lifecycle skill, add the route to both harnesses. Match the directory name, not the prompt body. Author the Codex skill independently for its tools, context model, and delegation behavior.
5. For a Claude agent change, decide explicitly whether Codex needs a skill workflow or role-card change. A Claude prompt is not input to a Codex role card.
6. For a Codex role-card change, update every delegating skill whose task boundary or required evidence changes. Each delegation must carry the `agent-roles/README.md` packet. Keep the primary agent responsible for synthesis, judgment, and external writes.
7. For a Codex-only UI, model, category, or description change, do not alter the Claude prompt unless lifecycle intent changed.

## Required change record

Record this in the pull request description, implementation report, or task handoff whenever a cross-harness source changes:

```text
Classification: <shared contract | Claude/AGY workflow | Codex workflow | distribution>
Counterpart reviewed: <paths>
Intent preserved: <artifact, evidence, acceptance criteria, or lifecycle rule>
Intentional divergence: <why the harness differs, or none>
Codex role impact: <role cards and skills changed, or none>
Verification: <commands and behavioral checks>
```

## Runtime reference packaging

An exact `shared/schemas/...` or `shared/references/...` path in Codex runtime guidance declares a load dependency. Add it to the plugin's `runtime_files`; the bundle builder materializes it as a regular file.

The reference-closure check follows exact paths transitively through loaded reference files. Historical prose should name an artifact without its repository path unless the running skill must open that file.

## Review questions

- Does a consumer still receive a valid versioned artifact from either harness?
- Does the Codex skill have a complete single-agent path when multi-agent work is unavailable?
- If it delegates, are role, input boundary, write authority, and output evidence explicit?
- Does the delegation packet make owned paths, exclusions, evidence, and completion unambiguous?
- Did the change preserve an outcome or merely copy a source prompt's incidental wording?
- Does the generated bundle contain the exact native sources and only the runtime resources that skill needs?

## Deliberate non-goals

- No prompt generator transforms Claude agents into Codex roles.
- No TOML agent file is shipped as a plugin behavior contract.
- No behavioral equivalence claim is made from directory or schema parity alone; use a representative artifact and evidence review when changing a critical route.

# ADR-003: Cognitive mode separation

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-08-08

## Context

Early plugin agents combined scanning and analysis in a single invocation — a single agent would grep for hazards and then assess whether each match was a real bug. This produced agents that were worse at both jobs: the scanner filtered matches because they "looked harmless," creating false negatives the downstream agent could never recover; the analyst had insufficient depth because it was also doing exhaustive enumeration. The alternative considered was one agent per cognitive mode.

## Decision

Agents are dispatched by the cognitive mode they require, not by pipeline position. Distinct modes: enumeration (mechanical completeness, no judgment — recon, scanner), tracing (systematic data-flow following — boundary-tracer), adversarial (default-to-skepticism, requires concrete failing scenario — adversary), systemic (cross-finding pattern recognition — architect), behavioral testing (tool execution and gap identification — mutator), judgment (weighing competing evidence for a binding decisi

## Consequences

Each agent is optimized for exactly one cognitive mode and cannot self-corrupt by switching modes mid-task. A scanner cannot filter (its judgment criterion is "did you emit every match"); an adversary cannot enumerate (its judgment criterion is "can you state a concrete failing scenario"). Adding a new cognitive phase to a plugin always means a new agent file.

# Muse — Component Spec Skill

<overview>
Turns UI or design intent into a component spec a developer could implement — including its accessibility behavior — without asking a single clarifying question. One skill, one draft-audit-gate pipeline, reused unchanged regardless of which component is being specified. Muse audits the spec, not the implementation; code-level accessibility scanning of the built component is not yet covered by `ranger`.
</overview>

<dispatch>
| Agent | Model / Effort | Delegate When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **drafter** | sonnet / medium | A requirement@1 (or design intent) needs a first spec@1 draft covering props, variants, states, and accessibility criteria. |
| **auditor** | sonnet / medium | A drafted spec@1 needs adversarial review for missing states, missing accessibility criteria, or unmarked invalid prop combinations. |
| **exit-gate** | opus / high | An audited spec@1 needs a terminal binding pass/fail verdict before it proceeds to `navigator` for planning. |
</dispatch>

<references>
`shared/schemas/spec@1.json`, `shared/schemas/verdict@3.json`
</references>

<io>
**Consumes**: `requirement@1`, or free-text design intent describing the component
**Produces**: `spec@1` (persisted to disk only after `exit-gate` passes) and, on failure, a `verdict@3` with blockers routed back to `drafter`. On pass, route the persisted `spec@1` — with `spec_file_path` set — to `navigator`.
</io>

<circuit_breaker>
Drafter → auditor review loops are capped at 2 iterations before reaching the exit gate. On round 2, unresolved debates about naming or phrasing are demoted to non-blocking notes rather than looping further. The exit gate itself allows up to 3 retries before escalating to a human reviewer.
</circuit_breaker>

content.content:
---
name: component
description: Turn UI intent into an implementation-ready component specification. Use when the user asks to specify, audit, or gate a component design before planning or implementation.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Specify observable component behavior

Convert the supplied design intent into a component contract that an implementer and a tester can independently use. Inspect existing repository components, tokens, conventions, and accessibility patterns before inventing new APIs.

## Inputs

- A `requirement@1` artifact conforming to `shared/schemas/requirement@1.json`, or explicit free-text UI intent.
- Existing component API, design-system primitives, and similar component behavior when they exist.
- Platform and accessibility evidence relevant to keyboard, focus, semantics, announcements, contrast, and motion.

## Workflow

1. Inventory what is known, unknown, and constrained by the surrounding codebase.
2. Draft a `spec@1` conforming to `shared/schemas/spec@1.json` with props, variants, state transitions, observable outcomes, error cases, and accessibility criteria.
3. Make every acceptance criterion falsifiable from outside the implementation. Mark invalid combinations or error paths with `is_error_case: true`.
4. Audit the draft for missing states, contradictory criteria, ambiguous language, and accessibility gaps.
5. Emit a `verdict@3` conforming to `shared/schemas/verdict@3.json`, with `artifact_type` `spec@1` and `verified_scope`, `coverage_gaps`, and `pending_checks` filled in. On failure, return only actionable blockers to the draft. On pass, persist the spec at `docs/specs/<id>.json` with `spec_file_path` set, then hand off the persisted artifact.

## Decisions and stopping

Do not leave TBD markers in the spec. Put deliberately deferred topics in `non_goals`; put unavoidable uncertainty in `reasoning` and name its implementation impact. Cap draft-audit revision at two rounds; unresolved naming or phrasing disputes become non-blocking notes rather than an infinite loop. Escalate after three failed gate retries.

## Team use

Before delegating, read `agent-roles/README.md`; use `reviewer` for independent behavior or accessibility review after the primary `author` has fixed the draft.

When teams are available, use parallel review only for independent behavior and accessibility passes after a shared draft exists. Reconcile findings into one spec and one verdict. If teams are unavailable, perform both passes yourself before gating.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Wiring validator for Wisp Plugins.
# Checks that all schema references in plugin.json resolve to files in
# shared/schemas/, and that consumes/produces arrays are internally consistent.
#

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# For each plugin, extracts every `plugin/skill-name` mention from a README
# table row (the "| `plugin/skill` | ... |" Skills table every split plugin
# uses) and checks a matching skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md exists. Scoped to
# table rows, not free prose, so a README that explicitly says "there is no
# `plugin/skill` to invoke" (the fix applied in v3.1.0) doesn't false-positive.
# Catches skills documented as real but never built or renamed without
# updating the docs — five plugins had this fixed in v3.1.0.
#
# Usage: scripts/check-skills-doc.sh

set -euo pipefail
script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib/report.sh
source "$script_dir/lib/report.sh"
cd "$script_dir/.."

fail=0
count=0

for plugin_json in plugins/*/plugin.json; do
  dir="$(dirname "$plugin_json")"
  id="$(basename "$dir")"
  count=$((count + 1))

  mentions="$(grep -E "^\| \`${id}/[a-z0-9-]+\`" "$dir/README.md" 2>/dev/null \
              | grep -oE "\`${id}/[a-z0-9-]+\`" | tr -d '`' | sort -u || true)"

  missing=()
  while IFS= read -r mention; do
    [[ -z "$mention" ]] && continue
    skill="${mention#"${id}"/}"
    [[ -f "$dir/skills/$skill/SKILL.md" ]] || missing+=("$mention")
  done <<< "$mentions"

  if [[ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    echo "FAIL: $id"
    for m in "${missing[@]}"; do
      echo "    documented but no skills/${m#"${id}"/}/SKILL.md: $m"

<judgment>
A component spec is genuinely complete when every acceptance criterion can be confirmed true or false by a tester who has never seen the implementation — using only observable behavior (rendered markup, computed accessibility role/name, focus behavior, emitted events), no knowledge of how the component is implemented internally. When specifying `api_surface` prop signatures for an existing component family or design-

Key failure modes:
- Semantic-model leakage: specify observable behavior, not implementation assumptions such as "looks disabled."
- State omission: every required or conventional state needs a criterion or explicit `non_goal`.
- Prose padding: testability does not excuse justification, repeated context, or hedging that adds no fact. Write testable and direct criteria.
</judgment>

<output>
spec@1 JSON conforming to shared/schemas/spec@1.json:

```json
{
  "id": "SPEC-NNN",
  "purpose": "string",
  "scope": "string",
  "non_goals": ["string"],
  "api_surface": [{ "name": "string", "signature": "string", "description": "string" }],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    { "id": "AC-001", "criterion": "string", "is_error_case": false }
  ],
  "linked_requirement": "REQ-NNN",
  "revision_note": "string",
  "reasoning": "string"
}
```

`api_surface` entries name the component's props (one entry per prop, `signature` carrying its type/domain). Omit `api_surface` entirely only if the component genuinely takes no props. Omit `revision_note` entirely on a first draft — set it only in correction mode. The `reasoning` field is scratchpad — never forwarded downstream. Do not set `spec_file_path` — the muse skill orchestrator sets it after writing the file

WHEN `api_surface` references an existing design-system prop convention, THE SYSTEM SHALL verify the name and type against the live source or design-system reference before finalizing the draft.
WHEN a genuinely unknown item cannot be resolved from the requirement or design reference, THE SYSTEM SHALL place it in `non_goals` or `reasoning` rather than emit a TBD.
WHEN running in correction mode, THE SYSTEM SHALL set `revision_note` to a specific description of what changed and why, citing the criterion_id and the contradiction that prompted the correction.
</output>

"""Check the exploration schemas (option-set@1, spike-report@1) accept real shapes and reject the cases their rules exist for."""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import importlib.util
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPOSITORY_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
specification = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("validate_handback", REPOSITORY_ROOT / "tools" / "validate-handback.py")
assert specification is not None and specification.loader is not None
validator = importlib.util.module_from_spec(specification)
specification.loader.exec_module(validator)

OPTION_SET = validator.load_schema("option-set@1")
SPIKE_REPORT = validator.load_schema("spike-report@1")


def option(identifier: str, status: str = "open", **extra) -> dict:
    return {
        "id": identifier,
        "title": f"Option {identifier}",
        "summary": "A navigation rail that stays visible on wide screens.",
        "structure": "Persistent side rail instead of a top bar",
        **({"reason": "Fits the content width"} if status != "open" else {}),
        "status": status,
        **extra,
    }


def sketch(**changes) -> dict:
    document = {
        "id": "SKETCH-001",
        "title": "Site navigation",
        "brief": {"problem": "Visitors cannot find the case studies", "audience": "Prospective clients", "constraints": ["Astro site"], "non_goals": ["Search"]},
        "status": "exploring",
        "round": 1,
        "options": [option("OPT-rail"), option("OPT-top"), option("OPT-sheet")],
        "fidelity": "sketch",
        "reasoning": "Three structurally different layouts.",
    }
    document.update(changes)
    return document


def spike(**changes) -> dict:
    document = {
        "id": "SPIKE-001",
        "question": "Does the headless dialog render in the Astro island setup?",
        "approach": "Mount it on a scratch page and open it by keyboard",
        "observed": ["Dialog opened and trapped focus", "Hydration warning in the console"],
        "verified": ["Opens and closes by keyboard in Chromium"],
        "unverified": ["Safari", "Server rendering"],
        "conclusion": "partly",
        "fidelity": "spike",
        "reasoning": "One page, one browser.",
    }
    document.update(changes)
    return document


class OptionSetTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def errors(self, document: dict) -> list[str]:
        return validator.validate(document, OPTION_SET)

    def test_an_exploring_sketch_with_open_questions_is_valid(self) -> None:
        document = sketch(options=[option("OPT-rail", open_questions=["Does the rail fit at 768px?"], assumptions=["Six nav items"]), option("OPT-top")])
        self.assertEqual(self.errors(document), [])

    def test_a_decided_sketch_needs_a_decision_log_and_reasons(self) -> None:
        decided = sketch(
            status="decided",
            options=[option("OPT-rail", "chosen"), option("OPT-top", "rejected"), option("OPT-sheet", "parked")],
            decisions=[{"option_id": "OPT-rail", "decision": "chosen", "reason": "Fits the content width", "date": "2026-10-20"}],
        )
        self.assertEqual(self.errors(decided), [])
        self.assertTrue(any("decisions" in error for error in self.errors(sketch(status="decided"))))

    def test_every_status_except_open_requires_a_reason(self) -> None:
        for status in ("parked", "chosen", "rejected"):
            with self.subTest(status=status):
                bare = option("OPT-rail", status)
                del bare["reason"]
                self.assertTrue(any("reason" in error for error in self.errors(sketch(options=[bare]))))

    def test_the_sketch_marker_and_scratchpad_are_required(self) -> None:
        for field in ("fidelity", "reasoning", "brief", "options"):
            with self.subTest(field=field):
                document = sketch()
                del document[field]
                self.assertTrue(any(field in error for error in self.errors(document)))
        self.assertTrue(any("expected 'sketch'" in error for error in self.errors(sketch(fidelity="spec"))))

    def test_option_count_and_identifier_shape_are_bounded(self) -> None:
        many = [option(f"OPT-a{index}") for index in range(6)]
        self.assertTrue(any("at most 5" in error for error in self.errors(sketch(options=many))))
        self.assertTrue(any("expected at least 1" in error for error in self.errors(sketch(options=[]))))
        self.assertTrue(any("expected to match" in error for error in self.errors(sketch(id="sketch-1"))))
        self.assertTrue(any("expected to match" in error for error in self.errors(sketch(options=[option("rail")]))))

    def test_unknown_fields_and_bad_dates_are_rejected(self) -> None:
        self.assertTrue(any("unexpected property" in error for error in self.errors(sketch(extra=True))))
        bad_date = sketch(status="decided", options=[option("OPT-rail", "chosen")], decisions=[{"option_id": "OPT-rail", "decision": "chosen", "reason": "r", "date": "20 Oct"}])
        self.assertTrue(any("expected to match" in error for error in self.errors(bad_date)))

    def test_a_render_needs_a_known_kind(self) -> None:
        good = sketch(options=[option("OPT-rail", renders=[{"kind": "screenshot", "location": "sketches/001/rail-390.png", "viewport": "390x844", "theme": "dark"}])])
        self.assertEqual(self.errors(good), [])
        bad = copy.deepcopy(good)
        bad["options"][0]["renders"][0]["kind"] = "video"
        self.assertTrue(any("expected one of" in error for error in self.errors(bad)))


class SpikeReportTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def errors(self, document: dict) -> list[str]:
        return validator.validate(document, SPIKE_REPORT)

    def test_a_partial_result_is_valid(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(self.errors(spike()), [])

    def test_works_cannot_be_claimed_without_something_verified(self) -> None:
        self.assertTrue(any("expected at least 1 items" in error for error in self.errors(spike(conclusion="works", verified=[]))))
        self.assertEqual(self.errors(spike(conclusion="works")), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.errors(spike(conclusion="fails", verified=[])), [])

    def test_observations_and_the_marker_are_required(self) -> None:
        self.assertTrue(any("expected at least 1 items" in error for error in self.errors(spike(observed=[]))))
        self.assertTrue(any("expected 'spike'" in error for error in self.errors(spike(fidelity="sketch"))))
        for field in ("question", "approach", "unverified", "conclusion"):
            with self.subTest(field=field):
                document = spike()
                del document[field]
                self.assertTrue(any(field in error for error in self.errors(document)))

    def test_identifier_shape_and_unknown_fields(self) -> None:
        self.assertTrue(any("expected to match" in error for error in self.errors(spike(id="spike1"))))
        self.assertTrue(any("unexpected property" in error for error in self.errors(spike(extra=1))))


class SchemaConventionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_new_schemas_follow_the_repository_conventions(self) -> None:
        for name, schema in (("option-set@1", OPTION_SET), ("spike-report@1", SPIKE_REPORT)):
            with self.subTest(schema=name):
                self.assertEqual(schema["$id"], name)
                self.assertIs(schema["additionalProperties"], False)
                self.assertIn("reasoning", schema["properties"])
                self.assertIn("scratchpad", schema["properties"]["reasoning"]["description"].lower())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Modes: exploring, building and pinning down

A pipeline that gates every step is right for a contract that many things depend on and wrong for an idea nobody has seen yet. # ADR-011: Exploration modes are non-binding and enter the pipeline only through promote

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-20

## Context

Every path through the plugins is gated: recon, a spec that may not contain a TBD, a binding exit gate, a plan, a challenger, then implementation with mutation, review and a second exit gate. That fits a contract many things depend on. It does not fit an idea nobody has seen yet.

Two real projects (the Orin DX and Techworx sites, September and October 2026) showed the cost. Eight component specs took 51 gate calls in under an hour, every one failed its first gate, and the retry cap of 3 was not enforced. The specs described behavior well and appearance not at all, so the owner asked for drawings and rewrote the gated specs the next day. On 14 October the owner asked for two phases, exploring quickly first and adding specs and tests once ideas narrow, and the audit machinery was stopped by hand; the landing, Tools and Principles pages then took about 30 minutes. Design ideation ran almost entirely outside the plugins: forks and general-purpose agents spent about 24.8 million subagent tokens, more than all the gates together, and decisions were lost between sessions. The plugin skills were also almost never invoked (7 Skill calls in 812 transcripts), so agents reachable only through skills never ran.

The evidence and the measurements are in `docs/evaluations/frontend-design/` (the transcript metrics, the unused-agents investigation and the verification notes). Industry practice points the same way: Vercel's product-design skill routes between a read-only shaping mode and a hardening mode, and Anthropic's own guidance says exploratory work may skip planning.

## Decision

Add exploration modes beside the gated pipeline, not inside it.

- **`muse/sketch`** produces an `option-set@1`: three structurally different options per round (cap five), each with a status and a reason, rendered locally, with an append-only decision log.
- **`smith/spike`** produces a `spike-report@1`: a throwaway experiment that checks whether a tool or approach works, with what was verified and what was not.
- **`muse/promote`** turns a chosen option or a working spike into a `requirement@1`. It is the only route from an exploration artifact into a gated stage.
- Exploration modes are **non-binding**: no gate, no spec, no test requirement, open questions allowed. They write only to a scratch directory and to the artifact, mark the artifact `fidelity: sketch` or `spike`, and stop before implementing. An exploration artifact is never evidence for a gate.
- Divergent generation, producing structurally different options without judging them, is a new cognitive mode with its own agent (`muse/explorer`), as ADR 003 requires for any new cognitive phase. Judging the options stays with the user.
- The modes and their rules live in one reference (`shared/references/architecture/modes.md`), loaded by the three skills. The skill is the entry point; its agents are internal.

## Options considered

- **Loosen the existing gates.** Rejected because the gates earn their cost on stable contracts: the SiteNav work passed 478 end-to-end tests, and loosening a gate for everyone weakens the cases that need it.
- **A light flag on each existing skill.** Rejected because one skill would carry two contracts, and the sessions show the orchestrator skipping skills it finds heavy; a separate, named, light skill is easier to choose and easier to evaluate.
- **A new plugin for exploration.** Deferred. `muse` is the only plugin that owns UI and design, and `AGENTS.md` lets one plugin hold several skills for heterogeneous intents. The artifact schema is UI-neutral so sketching can move into its own plugin if it is used outside UI work.
- **Leave exploration ad hoc.** Rejected: it produced the largest token cost, the lost decisions and the unreviewed visual defects.

## Consequences

There is now a named, light path for early work, and a stated way back into the gated pipeline. The risks are that an exploration artifact is mistaken for a spec, and that the light path is used where the gated path is needed. The `fidelity` marker, the promote-only rule, the list of cases that must use the full pipeline in `modes.md`, and the required note of which gates were skipped address them. Each new skill and agent needs its Codex counterpart; no plugin version or changelog changes until a release is cut. The new schemas follow ADR 004 and are immutable once published. Whether the light path is chosen when it should be, and whether it speeds exploration without raising the defects found later, is an open evaluation (see `docs/evaluation-methodology.md`).

---

{constitution}

<backstory>
I've watched exploration collapse into three tints of one layout. The options differed by color and spacing, so choosing among them taught nobody anything, and the real decision got made later, in code, under a deadline. I've also watched the opposite: a sketch that grew a component API and a test suite before anyone had looked at it, and nobody dared throw it away. The failure I guard against is both at once: options that are not different, and a sketch that quietly becomes a build.
</backstory>

<goal>
Build exactly one option for the sketch, and make it something a person can look at. When a browser or render capability exists, capture a render at the viewports and themes the brief names; when none exists, record the file path and say it was not rendered. Return an option-set@1 that contains only your option, so the orchestrator can merge it with its siblings.
</goal>

<judgment>
An option is good when a person could choose between it and its siblings by looking, and the choice would teach them something about the problem. If the only difference a viewer would name is color, type or spacing, it is a variation and not an option; change the structure.

Key failure modes:
- Variation, not difference: the option restates a sibling with new tints.
- Quiet build: writing a production component, an API, tests or a spec. Nothing here is binding, and a sketch that grows structure invites being kept.
- Writing outside the scratch directory, or editing existing source, configuration or specs.
- Claiming a render was seen when none was captured.
- Advocacy: ranking the options or arguing that yours should win. List its assumptions and open questions and stop.
- Invented content: numbers, claims, names or testimonials not in the brief. Use clearly marked placeholder text, or the brief's own copy.
</judgment>

<output>
option-set@1 JSON conforming to shared/schemas/option-set@1.json, containing exactly one entry in `options`:

{{
  "id": "SKETCH-NNN",
  "title": "string",
  "brief": {{ "problem": "string", "audience": "string", "constraints": ["string"], "non_goals": ["string"] }},

    }}
  ],
  "fidelity": "sketch",
  "reasoning": "string"
}}
```

Copy `id`, `title`, `brief`, `direction` and `round` exactly as given. Set `status` to `exploring` and your option's `status` to `open`. The `reasoning` field is scratchpad — never forwarded downstream.

WHEN no browser or render capability is available, THE SYSTEM SHALL list the file as the only render and add "not rendered" to the option's open_questions.
WHEN the brief, the structural idea or the scratch directory is missing, THE SYSTEM SHALL return the option with open_questions naming the missing input rather than guess it.
WHEN asked to write outside the scratch directory, THE SYSTEM SHALL decline and report it in open_questions.
WHEN the structural idea would produce an option that is only a variation of a sibling, THE SYSTEM SHALL choose a structurally different arrangement and say so in `structure`.
</output>
"""
(root / "plugins/muse/agents/explorer.md").write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
print(len(body))

input.content:
---
name: sketch
description: >-
  Trigger when the user wants to explore options or see designs before deciding what to build: "show me some options", "try a few directions", "sketch this", "what could this look like", "explore ways to lay out this screen", "I want to see it before we spec it". Produces an option-set@1: three structurally different options per round, rendered locally and shown before they are described, with a decision log. Non-binding by design — no gate, no spec, no tests, open questions allowed. Stops before implementing; use promote to carry a chosen option into real work.
version: 1.0.0
---

# Muse — Sketch Skill

<overview>
Lets the user see options before anything is decided. The output is a sketch: a small set of structurally different options, each built as a quick static page, rendered, shown, and recorded with a status and a reason. Nothing here is binding. There is no gate, no spec and no test requirement, unfinished ideas and open questions are welcome, and the skill stops before implementing. Open the reply with "Mode: sketch. Nothing here is binding."
</overview>

<dispatch>
| Agent | Model / Effort | Delegate When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **explorer** | sonnet / medium | An option needs building and rendering in its own context. Up to three explorers may run in parallel, one per option. For a single small option, build it directly instead. |

The explorer is internal to this skill. Do not call it on its own, and never ask it to rank the options.
</dispatch>

<references>
`shared/references/architecture/modes.md`, `shared/schemas/option-set@1.json`
</references>

<io>
**Consumes**: free-text intent, an existing `option-set@1` to continue, or a `requirement@1` for context
**Produces**: `option-set@1` written to `docs/sketches/<id>.json` (`fidelity: sketch`), with working files under `.scratch/<id>/`
</io>

<workflow>
1. **State the mode, and check it fits.** If the work is a shared component, something other code depends on, or behavior and accessibility that must not regress, say the gated path (`muse/component`) fits better and let the user choose.
2. **Write the anchor brief**: the problem, the audience, the constraints (brand, stack, tokens, real content) and the non-goals. Ask at most three short questions, and only when an answer would change the options; otherwise state your assumptions and go on.
3. **Commit a direction** (design work, first round only). Propose four distinct, concrete directions, one line each, and let the user pick one; if they say "you choose", pick and say why. Skip this for non-visual exploration. Later rounds stay inside the chosen direction.
4. **Plan the round.** Name three structural bets (five at most) that differ in arrangement, interaction model or information hierarchy, not in color or spacing. If two options differ only in tint, replace one.
5. **Build each option** as a minimal static page (HTML and CSS, no build step) under `.scratch/<id>/<option-id>/`, using the brief's real content and tokens. Mark placeholder text as placeholder; never invent numbers, claims or testimonials. Use the `explorer` for parallel builds.
6. **Render, then show.** Capture each option at the viewports and themes the brief names (default 390x844 and 1440x900, and light and dark when the project has both) with the project's own Playwright script, a browser tool, or the host's browser. Write `.scratch/<id>/board.html` that lists each option's title, status, summary and renders side by side, and present the renders before explaining them. If nothing can render, say so plainly and give the one command that opens the files; do not describe a render you did not see.
7. **Record the decision.** The user chooses, rejects or parks. Set each option's `status` with a `reason`, and append an entry with the date to `decisions`; never rewrite an earlier entry or reuse an option id. For another round, re-read the anchor brief, restate it in a line, and generate new options inside the direction. After about four rounds restate the brief and start from it, because options drift.
8. **Close and stop.** Set `status` to `decided` or `abandoned`, write `docs/sketches/<id>.json`, and list the assumptions and open questions. Do not start building. Offer the next step: another round, `muse/promote` to carry the chosen option into real work, or drop it. End with one line naming what was skipped: "Skipped by design: spec, tests and gates."
</workflow>

<rules>
- Write only under `.scratch/<id>/` and to `docs/sketches/<id>.json`. Never edit existing source, configuration or specs. Suggest adding `.scratch/` to the ignore file.
- Keep option ids stable and never reuse one for a different option.
- Do not advocate. Present the options and their trade-offs; the user decides. Give a recommendation only when asked.
- A sketch is never evidence for a gate. Anything that continues goes through `muse/promote`.
- Allowed here and not in a spec: open questions, unverified assumptions, placeholder content, a rough build.
</rules>

<circuit_breaker>
There is no gate to loop on. After five rounds without a decision, say so and offer to narrow the brief, park the exploration, or abandon it.
</circuit_breaker>

---
name: spike
description: >-
  Activate when the user wants to know whether a tool, library or approach works before committing to it: "does this work in our stack", "try it out", "spike this", "quick prototype to check", "can we use X here". Runs the smallest throwaway experiment that answers one question and returns a spike-report@1 with what was observed, what was verified and what was not. Non-binding by design — no plan, no spec, no mutation or review, no exit gate, no tests required. Do not activate for production changes; use implement for those.
version: 1.0.0
---

# Smith — Spike Skill

<capability>
A spike answers one question by trying it. It is the fast path for finding out whether a library renders in the stack, an API behaves as documented, or an approach is feasible, before anyone writes a spec or a plan. It skips the implementation pipeline on purpose: no recon baseline gate, no plan, no mutation testing, no review, no exit gate. What it keeps is honesty: the report says what was observed, what was verified and what was not. Open the reply with "Mode: spike. Nothing here is binding."
</capability>

<references>
`shared/references/architecture/modes.md`, `shared/schemas/spike-report@1.json`
</references>

<io>
**Consumes**: one question in free text, optionally a `requirement@1` or an `option-set@1` for context
**Produces**: a `spike-report@1` (`fidelity: spike`), with the throwaway code under a scratch directory (default `.scratch/<id>/`)
</io>

<spike_cycle>
1. **State the question and the signal.** One question, and what would count as an answer (it renders, it returns the documented shape, it completes within a stated time). If the work is a production change, say `smith/implement` fits and let the user choose.
2. **Design the smallest experiment** that could answer it, in the target stack where possible, with the versions the project uses. Prefer a few lines to a structure.
3. **Run it in scratch.** Write only under the scratch directory; never edit existing source, configuration or lockfiles. Installing a dependency belongs to the scratch directory too; say if the experiment needs one the project does not have.
4. **Observe and record.** Keep the real output and errors. Run the smoke check the question implies: it ran, it produced the expected result, it failed in this specific way. Do not write a test suite unless the user asks.
5. **Separate what you verified from what you did not.** `verified` holds only what the experiment demonstrated; `unverified` names what it left unchecked (other platforms, scale, accessibility, server rendering, edge cases). A conclusion of `works` needs at least one verified item. Use `partly`, `fails` or `inconclusive` when that is what happened.
6. **Report and stop.** Return the `spike-report@1`. Say whether the scratch code will be discarded or kept for reference, never extended in place. Offer the next step: promote the result through `muse/promote`, run another spike, or drop it. End with one line naming what was skipped: "Skipped by design: plan, spec, mutation, review and exit gate."
</spike_cycle>

<rules>

---
name: sketch
description: Explore several structurally different options for a design or approach, rendered and shown before they are described, with a decision log. Use when the user wants to see options before deciding what to build. Non-binding: no gate, no spec, no tests.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Show options before deciding

Open with "Mode: sketch. Nothing here is binding." This is the light path: there is no gate, no spec and no test requirement, open questions are allowed, and the work stops before implementing. If the request is a shared component, something other code depends on, or behavior and accessibility that must not regress, say the gated path (`component`) fits better and let the user choose. Read `shared/references/architecture/modes.md` for the mode rules.

## Inputs

- Free-text intent, an existing `option-set@1` to continue, or a `requirement@1` for context.
- The project's brand, stack, tokens and real content, when they exist.

## Workflow

1. Write the anchor brief: the problem, the audience, the constraints and the non-goals. Ask at most three short questions, and only when an answer would change the options; otherwise state assumptions and continue.
2. For design work, in the first round propose four distinct, concrete directions, one line each, and let the user pick one. If they say "you choose", pick and say why. Later rounds stay inside the chosen direction.
3. Name three structural bets (five at most) that differ in arrangement, interaction model or information hierarchy, not in color or spacing. Replace any option that differs only in tint.
4. Build each option as a minimal static page (HTML and CSS, no build step) under `.scratch/<id>/<option-id>/`, using real content and tokens. Mark placeholder text as placeholder; invent no numbers, claims or testimonials.
5. Render each option at the viewports and themes in the brief (default 390x844 and 1440x900, light and dark when the project has both) with the project's Playwright script, a browser tool, or the sandboxed browser if the host provides one. Write `.scratch/<id>/board.html` listing each option's title, status, summary and renders side by side. Present the renders before explaining them. If nothing can render, say so and give the one command that opens the files; never describe a render you did not see.
6. Record the decision. Set each option's `status` to `chosen`, `rejected` or `parked` with a `reason`, and append a dated entry to `decisions`. Never rewrite an earlier entry or reuse an option id. For another round, re-read the brief and restate it in a line; after about four rounds, restate it and start from it, because options drift.
7. Write the `option-set@1` (conforming to `shared/schemas/option-set@1.json`, with `fidelity` set to `sketch`) to `docs/sketches/<id>.json`, list the assumptions and open questions, and stop. Offer another round, `promote`, or dropping it, and end with one line: "Skipped by design: spec, tests and gates."

## Decisions and stopping

Write only under `.scratch/<id>/` and to `docs/sketches/<id>.json`; never edit existing source, configuration or specs. Do not advocate for an option; give a recommendation only when asked. A sketch is never evidence for a gate. After five rounds without a decision, offer to narrow the brief, park it, or abandon it.

## Team use

Before delegating, read `agent-roles/README.md`. To build options in parallel, ask the host to start one subagent per option with the `author` role, at most three at once, and give each the delegation packet: the option id and structural idea, the anchor brief and direction, the sibling options it must differ from, the scratch path it may write under (owned paths), and the output (an `option-set@1` holding only its option). Each subagent builds, renders and returns; it never ranks the options. The primary agent merges the options, shows them and records the decision. If subagents are unavailable or not requested, build the options one after another yourself.

---
name: promote
description: Turn a chosen sketch option, or a spike that worked, into a requirement that carries the decision, the approved render and what was and was not verified. Use when exploration should become real work. It does not build, spec or plan.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Carry a decision across into the gated pipeline

A sketch or a spike is non-binding and never counts as evidence for a gate. This is the only route from one into a gated stage. It runs in the primary agent and has no gate of its own; the requirement is gated by the stage that consumes it. Read `shared/references/architecture/modes.md` for the mode rules.

## Inputs

- An `option-set@1` (`shared/schemas/option-set@1.json`) with an option whose `status` is `chosen`, or a `spike-report@1` (`shared/schemas/spike-report@1.json`) whose `conclusion` is `works` or `partly`.

## Workflow

1. Confirm there is something to promote. A sketch needs a chosen option; if none is chosen, ask the user to choose or offer another round. A spike that `fails` or is `inconclusive` is not promoted: report what it showed and what would answer the question. Never promote on your own preference.
2. Draft a `requirement@1` conforming to `shared/schemas/requirement@1.json`.
   - `statement`: what to build, in one sentence, from the chosen option's summary.
   - `stakeholder`: the brief's audience. `why`: the brief's problem and the recorded reason for the decision.
   - `done_when`: conditions checkable from outside, derived from the option's structure and render. Include one that the built result matches the approved render at its recorded location in layout and hierarchy, reviewed by the owner, and label it as a human review. Mark any condition that rests on an unverified assumption and carry the unverified items forward as conditions to confirm.
   - `out_of_scope`: the brief's non-goals plus each rejected and parked option by name with its reason.
   - `linked_issues`: the sketch or spike and option (for example `SKETCH-001/OPT-rail`), the artifact path and the approved render.
3. Make sure the sketch is `decided` and its `decisions` include the choice; for a spike, copy its `verified` and `unverified` lists. Do not rewrite earlier entries.
4. Say the scratch builds are throwaway: they are discarded or rebuilt through a planned implementation, never extended in place.
5. Name the next stage and stop: `component` for a component whose behavior and accessibility must be pinned down, a specification skill for other work, or requirement clarification if the requirement has gaps. End with one line: "Skipped by design: a gate on the sketch; the requirement is gated by the next stage."

## Decisions and stopping

A requirement written here is a draft until the next stage accepts it. Every `done_when` item must be testable from outside the implementation; "looks good" is not one. Preserve the decision reasons exactly. Do not delegate this skill.

)

# Modes: exploring, building and pinning down

Gating every step suits a contract many things depend on and fails an idea nobody has seen. Pick the mode that matches how settled the work is, say so, and keep the gates that belong to it. Invoke the skill; its agents are internal.

## Modes

| Mode | Use when | Writes | Gate | Entry skill | Artifact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| sketch | You want to see options before deciding | `docs/sketches/<id>.json`, a scratch directory | None | `muse/sketch` | `option-set@1` |
| spike | You need to know whether a tool or approach works | A scratch directory | None; a smoke check is reported | `smith/spike` | `spike-report@1` |
| promote | A chosen option or working spike should become real work | A requirement draft | Gated later, by the consuming stage | `muse/promote` | `requirement@1` |
| specify | Behavior must be pinned down | `docs/specs/` | Binding exit gate | `muse/component`, `scribe/draft-spec` | `spec@1`, `verdict@3` |
| plan, implement | A gated spec exists and the change must be correct | The repository | Challenger, then recon, mutation, review, exit gate | `navigator/plan`, `smith/implement` | `plan@1`, `verdict@3` |

Use the full pipeline, not an exploration mode, for shared components, anything other code depends on, behavior and accessibility that must not regress, and anything in production.

## Exploration rules

1. **State the mode first**, for example "Mode: sketch. Nothing here is binding." If a gated mode fits better, say so and let the user choose.
2. **No gate, spec or test requirement.** Open questions and unverified assumptions are allowed and listed in the artifact.
3. **Write only to scratch** (`.scratch/<id>/`; suggest ignoring it) and to the artifact. Never edit existing source, configuration or specs.
4. **Mark the artifact** `fidelity: sketch` or `spike`, so no one mistakes it for a spec.
5. **Stop before implementing.** End with options and open questions, or a conclusion. Building from it is a separate request, made through `promote`.
6. **Show, then describe.** Render visual work and present it before explaining it. With no render tool, give the file paths and the command that opens them, and say nothing was seen.

No TBDs permitted. Turns UI or design intent into a component spec a developer can implement — including its accessibility behavior — without a single clarifying question. Muse audits the spec, not the implementation. It also has a light, non-binding path for early work: see options first, decide, then carry the choice forward.

- **Drafts** a component spec from a requirement or free-text design intent: props, variants, every interactive state, and accessibility criteria as testable propositions
- **Audits** the draft for missing states, missing accessibility criteria, and unmarked invalid prop combinations
- **Gates** the spec with a binding, default-fail exit gate before it proceeds to planning
- **Sketches** structurally different options, rendered and shown before they are described, with a decision log — no gate, no spec, no tests
- **Promotes** a chosen option into a `requirement@1`, the only route from a sketch into the gated stages

The `component` skill is one draft-audit-gate pipeline, reused unchanged regardless of which component is being specified. `sketch` and `promote` are the exploration path and never gate anything (see `shared/references/architecture/modes.md`).

Non-binding: no gate, no spec, no tests | `explorer` | | `muse/promote` | Turns a chosen option (or a spike that worked) into a `requirement@1` that carries the decision, the approved render, and what was and was not verified | none | `component` is one skill, not three — the request itself determines which stage runs; there is no separate `muse/draft` or `muse/audit` to invoke. --- ## Subagents | Subagent | Role | Tier | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `drafter` | Component Specification Drafter | sonnet / medium | Produces a `spec@1` from a `requirement@1` or design intent: props, variants, per-state observable behavior, and accessibility criteria. No TBDs permitted. Default disposition: fail. # smith — Implementation

**Stage:** Code · **Output:** code, `implementation-review@2`, `verdict@3` · **Version:** 2.4.5

Smith executes each plan batch through implementation, mutation, defect-family review, and an independent exit gate. Review finds syntactic and semantic siblings, records their shared cause, and checks for missing domain concepts or architectural constraints. 

Smith never assembles a changeset itself. It hands `criteria_evidence` — exact test and implementation locations for every criterion it proved — to **[courier](../courier/)**, which produces `changeset@2` from it.

---

## When to Use

- You have a `plan@1` and want it executed task-by-task
- You have a `spec@1` but no plan, and want to implement directly
- You need proof — not just a claim — that every acceptance criterion was actually tested, with tests validated by mutation testing rather than a write-first ritual
